title.narrative: Increased capacities of employers' and workers' organizations to participate effectively in the development of social and labour policy

description.narrative:
The engagement of citizens in governance matters is pivotal for Kenya, as reflected in the 2010 Constitution, which mandates public participation in policy formulation across all levels of government. Recognizing this, the ILO aims to enhance the capacities of employers' and workers' organizations to effectively contribute to social and labor policies. This initiative seeks to address recent increases in industrial unrest, driven by inadequacies in labor market institutions and a lack of effective social dialogue.
Through strategic collaboration, this program focuses on strengthening statutory labor institutions, such as the National Labour Board and various Wages Councils, which play essential roles in fostering social dialogue and maintaining industrial peace. By enhancing the skills of social partners in dispute prevention and resolution, this initiative aims to improve trust among stakeholders and facilitate a more participatory approach to governance.
The beneficiaries of this program include employers, workers, and their organizations, enhancing their ability to advocate for fair labor practices. Key activities will include mentorship programs for workers’ representatives, training for paralegals, and increased outreach to County Governments on best labor practices. These efforts are expected to increase the representativeness and inclusiveness of both employers' and workers' organizations, ultimately leading to better labor market governance.
By reinforcing the tripartite dialogue framework and building the capacities of all involved stakeholders, the ILO aims to contribute to a more stable and equitable labor environment in Kenya, advancing the broader goals of sustained economic growth and social justice in alignment with Kenya’s Vision 2030.
